title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: The directors of the Company and all employees of the Group in all regions in which the Group operates directly or via joint venture. Bound by the insider trading prohibition, confidentiality, the Front Page Test and the ban on dealing in other companies' securities, but not by the blackout, approval, short-term, margin loan or hedging rules.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All key management personnel of the Company (including directors), as well as other persons who are likely to possess Inside Information regarding the Company; the Procedures give further guidance on who qualifies. Subject to blackout periods, prior approval for every dealing, the 12-month short-term and short-selling bans, the margin loan and encumbrance approval requirement, the hedging approval requirement and post-trade confirmation.

tiers.name: the Chair
tiers.description: Distinguished only for approval: requests from the Chair go to the Chair of the Audit Committee or, in their absence, the Chair of the Risk Management Committee.

tiers.name: any other Director (including the Managing Director)
tiers.description: Distinguished only for approval: requests go to the Chair or, in their absence, the Chair of the Audit Committee; a request from the Chair of the Audit Committee is referred to the Chair or, in their absence, the Chair of the Risk Management Committee.

tiers.name: any other Restricted Person
tiers.description: Non-director Restricted Persons; requests go to the Managing Director or, in their absence, the Group Chief Financial Officer.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: Persons connected with a Restricted Person, defined in the Procedures rather than the Policy. They are directly bound by the blackout, short-term, short-selling, margin loan, encumbrance and hedging rules, and the Restricted Person applies for approval on their behalf.

definitions.hedging_definition: Hedging includes entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Company securities (for example, entering into arrangements that have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with unvested securities issued pursuant to a staff or director equity plan).

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on the ASX on 30 June each year, or if that date is not a trading day, the last trading day before that day
windows.end_anchor: the day the full-year results announcement is released to ASX (dealing may occur the following day, subject to approval under section 5.4)

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on the ASX on 31 December each year, or if that date is not a trading day, the last trading day before that day
windows.end_anchor: the day the half-year results announcement is released to ASX

windows.start_anchor: any other period that the Board specifies from time to time

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other blackout period from time to time (section 5.1). Separately, the Company may notify Employees that they must not deal, either for a specified period or until further notice (section 4.1). The Policy does not state whether such periods are announced or confidential, but a refusal or withdrawal of approval must be kept confidential by the applicant.

rules.detail: There is no separate derivatives rule, but 'dealing' is defined to capture the full range of transactions, arrangements and financial products available in connection with the Company's securities, with an express substance over form approach and no venue limit. An OTC put and call is therefore a dealing needing prior written approval under section 5.4, and a hedging approval under 5.8, and is barred in blackout periods.
rules.evidence: When the expression 'deal' or 'dealing' is used in this Policy, it is intended to capture the full range of transactions, arrangements and financial products that are available in connection with a company's securities. ... The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.

rules.detail: Employees who are not Restricted Persons or Connected Persons are subject only to the insider trading prohibition, any Company notice not to deal, and the Front Page Test; sections 5.1 to 5.8 do not apply to them.
rules.evidence: Certain aspects of this Policy apply only to Restricted Persons and their Connected Persons.

rules.detail: Hedging Company securities is permitted with prior written approval, sought from the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary and determined by the relevant Approving Officer under section 5.5. There is no outright ban and no security-state limitation in the operative words.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons and Connected Persons must not, without prior written approval, hedge Company securities.

rules.detail: Unusually, the Policy does not absolutely prohibit hedging unvested plan securities; it gives that as the illustration of what counts as hedging and subjects it to the same prior written approval. Approval would still have to survive the Front Page Test and the terms of the relevant equity plan, which are outside the Policy.
rules.evidence: for example, entering into arrangements that have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with unvested securities issued pursuant to a staff or director equity plan

rules.detail: Section 5.8 binds only Restricted Persons and Connected Persons; hedging by other Employees is not addressed.

Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or collar-plus-loan limits the economic risk associated with holding Company securities and so needs hedging approval, and if secured it also needs approval under 5.7. The tension is section 5.2, which names forward contracts as an example of prohibited short-term dealing, so a monetisation structure must be long-dated to avoid that ban.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 12 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

rules.detail: Outright ban with no approval route, defined by reference to borrowing a security and selling it to buy back lower. The exceptional-circumstances relief in 5.3 covers only blackout and short-term dealing, not short selling.
rules.evidence: Short sell the Company's securities. Short selling refers to the practice of borrowing a security and selling it in the hope that it can be bought back at a lower price at some time in the future to close out the short position.

rules.detail: The short-selling ban in section 5.2 is addressed only to Restricted Persons and Connected Persons.

Securities lending arrangements are named in the chapeau to 5.7 and any dealing in connection with one requires prior written approval, treated under the section 5.5 process. Lending stock to facilitate a short position would still run into the 5.2 short-selling ban.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons and Connected Persons must obtain prior written approval for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending or securities lending arrangement

rules.detail: CFDs are not named. A CFD is a financial product available in connection with the Company's securities and so a dealing requiring approval, but a short CFD would breach the short-selling ban and a CFD closed within 12 months would breach the short-term dealing ban, so approval is unlikely.
rules.evidence: it is intended to capture the full range of transactions, arrangements and financial products that are available in connection with a company's securities

rules.detail: Margin lending is not banned. Entering into a margin lending arrangement, transferring securities into an existing margin loan account, and selling securities to satisfy a margin call each require prior written approval under the section 5.5 process.
rules.evidence: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account; selling securities in the Company to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan

rules.detail: Section 5.7 binds only Restricted Persons and Connected Persons.

The grant of a mortgage, charge, lien or other encumbrance or third party interest over Company securities is expressly listed as requiring prior written approval, not prohibited. The bullet is general in terms even though the chapeau frames 5.7 around margin lending and securities lending arrangements.
rules.evidence: the grant of a mortgage, charge, lien or other encumbrance or third party interest over the Company's securities.

rules.detail: No encumbrance rule applies to Employees who are not Restricted Persons or Connected Persons.

Secured financing over Company securities is permitted with prior written approval: the encumbrance bullet in 5.7(a) covers any mortgage, charge, lien, encumbrance or third party interest, and the Policy then carves the lender's enforcement sale out of the blackout, short-term and approval rules. Section 6 does not disapply 5.7 or 5.8, so approval for the arrangement itself is always needed.
rules.evidence: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: Secured financing is regulated only through section 5.7, which binds Restricted Persons and Connected Persons.

A twelve-month rule, far longer than the market-standard three months, and it reaches beyond on-market round trips to 'other short-term dealings', with forward contracts given as the example. Relief is available only on an exceptional-circumstances application under 5.3 (severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order). Participation in an equity plan is excluded from 5.2, but dealing in plan securities once they cease to be held under the plan is not.
rules.evidence: Deal in the Company's securities on a short-term trading basis. Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 12 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

rules.detail: The short-term dealing ban applies only to Restricted Persons and Connected Persons.

exemption_authority: The Approving Officer for the applicant (Chair of the Audit Committee for the Chair; the Chair for other Directors; the Managing Director or Group CFO for other Restricted Persons) may approve dealing in a blackout period or on a short-term basis in exceptional circumstances, and grants the margin loan, encumbrance and hedging approvals. The Board may set additional blackouts, and the directors may determine that the equity plan carve-outs operate differently. No approval may be granted where the dealing would fail the Front Page Test.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons and Connected Persons must obtain prior written approval for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending or securities lending arrangement, including ... the grant of a mortgage, charge, lien or other encumbrance or third party interest over the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Ramsay gates rather than bans secured financing, so the loan leg of a funded collar and the security over the collared shares are both available on a single prior written approval from the Approving Officer.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 5.1, 5.2 and 5.4 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale is excluded from the blackout, short-term and pre-approval rules, so lender enforcement does not put the executive in breach; the carve-out is not limited to margin lending.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons and Connected Persons must not, without prior written approval, hedge Company securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call legs are permitted on approval rather than banned, and the Policy does not carve unvested plan securities out of that approval route, which is unusually permissive.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 12 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The single biggest constraint on tenor: the collar should run well beyond 12 months and should not be documented as, or economically equivalent to, a short-dated forward, since forward contracts are the Policy's own example of a prohibited short-term dealing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 5.1, 5.2 and 5.4 of this Policy do not apply to: ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The excluded dealings list is expressed only against the blackout, short-term and pre-approval sections, so the margin loan, encumbrance and hedging approvals in 5.7 and 5.8 continue to apply to everything, including plan dealings and non-discretionary plans.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar cannot be documented around the rules; if its economic effect is a short position, a short-dated forward or an unapproved hedge, it will be treated as one.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An express reputational veto over the hedging and secured financing approvals, so the structure must be capable of clean public description and Appendix 3Y-style disclosure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the duration of the approval will be 5 business days ... The approval to deal can be withdrawn at any time by the Approving Officer in his/her absolute discretion without giving any reason ... it is recommended that Restricted Persons apply for approval to deal at least 2 business days prior to the intended date of dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing and execution must complete within five business days of approval, with two business days of lead time, and the bank bears the risk of unexplained withdrawal before signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Approving Officer may direct the person who is proposing to deal in the Company's securities not to deal, or impose conditions on the dealing in their discretion, and is not obliged to provide reasons for any direction or condition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval for the collar may carry unexplained conditions on tenor, size, strikes or disclosure that the confirmation and loan documents must accommodate.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Procedures provide further guidance around who is a Restricted Person and a Connected Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The perimeter of the approval regime, and who counts as a Connected Person for a family trust or controlled company, is set by an internal document the bank has not seen and should request.

bespoke_clauses.clause: selling securities in the Company to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan requires prior written approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A voluntary sale by the executive to meet a call needs fresh approval and may fall in a blackout, whereas a sale by the lender exercising its rights is excluded, so the facility should rely on lender enforcement rather than borrower top-up sales.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any person who breaches this Policy could face disciplinary action (including forfeiture of securities and/or suspension or termination of employment).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Forfeiture of plan securities is an express sanction, which would strip collateral out of the structure if the arrangement is later found non-compliant.

bespoke_clauses.clause: trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, where the Employee or a Connected Person did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a blackout period, the plan does not permit the Employee or a Connected Person to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to trading under the plan and the plan cannot be cancelled during a blackout period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Offers a route for physical settlement of the collar to occur without regard to blackout periods, if the settlement mechanics are pre-approved as a non-discretionary plan.

summary: A funded collar is achievable at Ramsay, subject to approvals and tenor. The Policy bans neither hedging nor secured financing: section 5.8 permits a Restricted Person or Connected Person to hedge Company securities with prior written approval, and section 5.7 permits the grant of a mortgage, charge, lien or other encumbrance or third party interest over Company securities, and entry into margin lending arrangements, on the same approval. Approval is given by the Chair for directors, the Chair of the Audit Committee for the Chair, and the Managing Director or Group CFO for other Restricted Persons, lasts only five business days, may be withdrawn at any time without reasons, may carry undisclosed conditions and will be refused if the dealing fails the Front Page Test; entry must be outside the 30 June and 31 December blackouts and any Board-specified period, and must be notified to the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary the same day. The critical constraint is section 5.2: short-term dealing covers a 12-month buy-and-sell window and expressly includes 'other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts)', so the collar must be long-dated and not economically a short-dated forward, and it must never be a short position. Helpfully, a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights is excluded from the blackout, short-term and pre-approval rules, so the bank's enforcement sale does not breach the Policy, though the approvals in 5.7 and 5.8 are never disapplied by the section 6 exclusions.
